texts: In 1867 Maxwell imagined a tiny being that opens a door only for fast molecules, sorting hot from cold for free - breaking the second law. The catch took a century to find: the demon must record each molecule, and erasing a bit of memory costs at least kT ln 2 of heat.

Information theory says the demon must pay to forget. Ours never forgets. Whether that is genius or a debt someone else will collect, I cannot say.$(br2)With enough $(item)Negentropy Cells$() and $(fluid)Dark Energy$() you can even reverse the heat death of a universe.
The $(item)Holographic Encoder$() writes a volume of matter onto its own boundary surface, per the holographic principle.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Day 61. The holographic principle: the most information a region can hold grows with its surface area, not its volume - a black hole's entropy is a quarter of its horizon area in Planck units. So a volume can, in principle, be written onto its own boundary. This machine does exactly that.

Built a demon of my own: the $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$(), a molecular gatekeeper that sorts fast particles from slow ones, defying the second law of thermodynamics.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.
By the books it should not work: sorting particles lowers entropy, and someone always pays. See my notes on Maxwell's Demon. For now I just watch it sort.
